title: Linux Systems Inspection
summary: Inspect an approved Linux sandbox and document relevant system state.
objectives: Use safe read-only inspection evidence from a sandbox.
Record system state without making unsupported conclusions.

vocab.def: The organized way an operating system stores files.
How much of a resource is currently in use.
An isolated environment for safe practice.

sections.heading: Observe before changing
sections.body: Approved commands and synthetic status files can show storage, memory, processes, and logs. The first responsibility is to observe and record.

sections.heading: Permission matters
sections.body: Do not use destructive deletion, privilege escalation, raw disk tools, shutdown commands, attack tools, or real network targets.

practice.prompt: A synthetic status file shows storage at 92%. What is the supported finding?
practice.answer: Storage utilization is high; the appropriate next step is to document and escalate or follow the approved procedure.

quiz.question: What is the safest first action when a sandbox system seems unusual?
options: Inspect approved status information and document it
quiz.answer: Inspect approved status information and document it

lab.objective: Inspect synthetic Linux status information and document a safe finding.

reflectionPrompt: What can a status record tell you, and what can it not prove?
